questions.q: How does the magnetic field of a current-carrying wire depend on distance?
questions.explain: B = μ₀·I/(2π·r): twice as far means half as strong.

questions.q: Why does twisting the power + and − reduce interference on the compass?
options: The fields of opposing currents cancel
Lower resistance of the wire pair
questions.explain: The fields of two conductors with opposite currents almost cancel each other.

questions.q: Which signal on board is the weakest and most vulnerable to radiated interference?
options: 2.4 GHz RC at the edge of range
questions.explain: The satellite signal is extremely weak; USB 3.0/HDMI/buck harmonics at 1.5 GHz drown it out.

questions.q: What does compassmot show in ArduPilot?
options: GPS quality with the motors running
questions.explain: The percentage of compass interference from motor current: > 30 % — move the compass.

questions.q: Symptom: RSSI is normal, LQ drops. The cause?
options: Wrong polarization of the radio's antenna
questions.explain: Wideband noise raises the reception threshold; RSSI can even rise from interference.

questions.q: How should a cable shield be grounded?
options: At both ends for better shielding
questions.explain: Grounding at both ends creates a loop through which the interference flows.

questions.q: Besides the satellite count, what should you look at on the GPS when you suspect interference?
options: The number of constellations in the settings
questions.explain: Interference lowers C/N0 before satellites drop out.

questions.q: Lines in the video that grow with throttle are a sign of:
options: Conducted ripple on the power supply
questions.explain: Lines on throttle are power supply ripple; “snow” is radiated interference.
